@aio:claude-auth: return only `{ user }` in the body — the tokens never appear there. `jwtAuth`
(`src/middlewares/jwtAuth.ts`) reads `accessToken` from the cookie jar. The `refreshToken`
cookie is scoped with `path: "/api/v1/auth/refresh"`, so it's only ever sent on that one
request, never leaking to every other endpoint. `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh` takes no body —
it reads its own cookie, checks it against the SHA-256 hash stored on the user row
(constant-time compare), rotates that hash with a compare-and-swap (`updateMany` filtered
by the hash just verified — so a stolen-and-replayed old token is rejected once it's been
rotated, and two concurrent refreshes with the same token can't both win), and re-sets both
cookies. Never bcrypt for this hash: it only reads 72 bytes, the same prefix for every JWT
of a user — bcrypt is for passwords only. Every refresh token carries a random `jti`, so two
signed in the same second are still different. `POST /api/v1/auth/logout` (behind
`jwtAuth`) clears both cookies and the stored
hash, revoking the session server-side. See `src/utils/authCookies.ts`.
client) with `credentials: "include"` in `ApiClientConfig` — without it, a browser drops
the cookies on any cross-origin request to the API.
